text:
maya: quick alert — us-west gpu pool 3 hit a saturation spike at ~09:14 UTC. queue depth from ~30 -> ~220 in ~90s, tail latency jumped, admission token refill stalled. anyone watching?

sam: saw it too. admission rate drops to near 0, then 429s start. looks like lots of tiny high-qps calls from a new customer batch.

leo: adding context: cluster node churn was low, network errors non-significant. this smells like admission/control-plane smoothing failing to throttle before pods full.

anika: confirmed traffic pattern: lots of parallel 1-2 token chat calls. short but very bursty. our scale-up hysteresis isn't catching these micro-bursts.

maya: here's the prom query I used to surface it:
```
max_over_time(queue_depth{pool="us-west-3"}[5m])
rate(admission_tokens_filled_total[1m])
```
queue depth jump is obvious. token refill drops as bursting drains reservoir.

sam: infra-bot, can you rate-limit the noisy tenant route for now? and apply a conservative admission debounce patch to prevent immediate refill empties? :pray:

infra-bot: action: temporary route rate-limit applied to tenant/alpha -> 60rps. TTL 30m. (reason: emergency backpressure) :rotating_light:

leo: thanks. longer-term we should avoid a single global reservoir being drained by many concurrent small requests. proposal: per-tenant per-pool token buckets + short debounce window on refill to smooth spikes. also add a small random jitter on scale-up triggers so we don't provision 40 nodes simultaneously.

anika: agree. also want to experiment with a small "burst_reservoir" buffer per host that can absorb short spikes without immediately triggering large scale-ups, combined with a slower refill and admission_debounce_ms.

sam: sample admission config snippet I sketched — can we test this in staging?
```yaml
admission_controller:
  token_bucket:
    global_capacity: 100000
    per_tenant_capacity: 2000
  refill:
    interval_ms: 500
    tokens_per_interval: 50
    debounce_ms: 3000  # wait before aggressive refill
  burst_reservoir_per_host: 150
  scale_policy:
    scale_up_cooldown_s: 60
    scale_down_grace_s: 300
    jitter_percent: 10
```

maya: nice. jitter_percent is important — we've seen simultaneous warm actions cause short-term admission collapse. any concerns about cost if we tune buffers bigger?

leo: cost vs availability tradeoff noted. we can put conservative defaults and let Optimize run post-deployment to suggest quantization/packing changes to offset cost. also, add a budget cap that prevents >X nodes in a single scale event unless manually approved.

anika: for testing plan: 1) deploy admission debounce + per-tenant buckets to staging, 2) run a synthetic burst test (5000 clients, 50k tiny reqs/s) with varying debounce, 3) measure queue depth, tail latency, and token refill curve, 4) run canary to prod with extra observability flags.

provision-bot: scheduled job created: staging-burst-test at 2026-03-19T02:00Z. notify: @maya @sam @anika.

sam: can someone add a grafana panel that plots token_inflight, queue_depth, and scale_events on same axis? will help correlate.

maya: on it. I'll add an alert: when queue_depth > 150 and token_refill_rate < 10r/s for >60s => create Sev3 and pause non-critical background scaling.

leo: final note: consider adding a tiny client-side exponential backoff recommendation for SDKs so we reduce the microburst pressure. docs + SDK patch could avoid 30% of these events.

maya: agreed. Action items: infra-bot rate-limit (done), deploy staging admission config (sam), create grafana panel + alert (maya), schedule canary (anika). I'll follow up after the staging run. :thumbsup:
